markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Invasive (61%)** · Ambiguous: InSitu vs Invasive · Careful review
InSitu (37%) stays in the 90% conformal set, though neighbors and MUSK favor Invasive. [F1]

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Invasive 61%, InSitu 37% | Invasive leads, not decisive |
| Conformal set | InSitu, Invasive | Cannot separate two classes |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.89 / 64th percentile | Input looks typical |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Same top class | Independent model agrees |
| Similar cases | 5 of 5 Invasive [F5] | Neighbors support Invasive |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (regions 0, 3, 10) · ↑ invasive · Strongest concept association with invasive carcinoma [F2] · Validated
- **Marked nuclear pleomorphism** (regions 0, 2, 4) · ↑ invasive · Scored well above typical [F3] · Validated
- **Scarce gland / tubule formation** (region 7) · ↑ invasive · Below typical overall; strongest in region 7, a low-risk region [F4] · Validated
- **Low duct-confined atypia** (region 11) · ↑ invasive · Below typical; concept model counts this toward invasive · Weak

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions cuts the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful.
- **Concepts**: Deletion difference 0.002 (CI −0.005 to 0.007) includes 0, so not shown to reflect the classifier. Mitoses and necrosis are Unreliable but contribute little here.

## Could be wrong if
- True class is InSitu (37%), and the duct-confined evidence is only Weak.
- Simulated stain degradation (severity 3) distorts features the models use.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 4, 11, 5**: highest classifier contribution; confirm invasion versus in situ.
2. **Regions 0, 3, 10**: tumor-infiltrating stroma; confirm true stromal invasion.
3. **Regions 7, 9**: lowest invasive scores; look for benign or in situ tissue.
